cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Don’t Go
cards.instruction: Create reasons another player must stay with you. Never directly ask them to stay.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your departure is not quite ready for my approval. Which tie will you wear to the interview?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The blue one. Can I have it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Blue is approved. Put it on; I need to see the knot before I release you into public.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A commendable shortcut. Now stand by the window. I haven't approved it in daylight.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 controls departure approval; A3 approves blue but requires knot inspection and A5 adds a light check without asking B to stay.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 tie choice causes A3 approval and fitting; B4 clip-on solves knot difficulty, so A5 shifts the same inspection to daylight.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants the chosen tie and B4 offers readiness, giving B a credible interview departure goal.

heightening.evidence: B4 shortcut could end the preparation; A5 praises it while making another appearance check necessary.

specificity.evidence: A1 interview and B2 blue tie establish a concrete departure and A's inspecting role.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 commendable shortcut earns its superior praise from B4 clip-on before redirecting that success into further scrutiny.
